steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Negative feedback: deviation -> correction (e.g. blood glucose, temp, water); Positive: amplifies (e.g. oxytocin in childbirth)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Kidney: cortex/medulla; nephron (Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct); ADH: increases water permeability of DCT/CD; Loop: counter-current multiplier creates medullary gradient

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Neurones: sensory, relay, motor; Resting potential -70mV (Na⁺/K⁺ pump, K⁺ leak); Action potential: depolarisation (Na⁺ in), repolarisation (K⁺ out), refractory period

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Synapse: Ca^2⁺ -> vesicle fusion -> neurotransmitter -> receptor -> depolarisation; Summation: temporal/spatial

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Describe how the loop of Henle creates a water potential gradient in the kidney medulla --- Solution: Descending limb: permeable to water, impermeable to ions -> water leaves by osmosis. Ascending limb: impermeable to water, active Na⁺/Cl⁻ transport out -> filtrate diluted, medulla concentrated. Counter-current multiplier: flow in opposite directions maintains gradient

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of homeostasis and the nervous system with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Describe how the loop of Henle creates a water potential gradient in the kidney medulla. Solution: Descending limb: permeable to water, impermeable to ions -> water leaves by osmosis. Ascending limb: impermeable to water, active Na⁺/Cl⁻ transport out -> filtrate diluted, medulla concentrated. Counter-current multiplier: flow in opposite directions maintains gradient Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and sup
